title: Investor asking yield and appreciation
buyer_primary_need: Assess whether Pearlmont offers a credible risk-adjusted rental investment over a 5–7 year holding period, comparing net performance after maintenance and vacancy with the buyer’s existing rentals. Key decision inputs include verified rental comparables, nearby competing supply, holding cost, and entry price.
key_information_learned: The buyer is an experienced small investor with existing rental properties.
The buyer is considering a 5–7 year hold, mainly for rental income but also for appreciation.
The buyer wants to model net yield after maintenance and vacancy, and values actual rental comparables and nearby supply more than facilities.
The buyer plans to verify rents, nearby pipeline, the maintenance fee, and current documents independently.
The buyer is pausing modelling until they can verify a dated Phase 1 document or itemised quote.
important_information_missed: After providing the simulator-verified starting price, the Agent could have connected it explicitly to the buyer’s entry-cost comparison and asked whether a viewing or location due diligence would be useful once the buyer’s independent checks are complete.

At turn 9, the Agent said it could not confirm the Phase 1 document source or date, although retrieved Knowledge identified the FAQ source and its stated update date. It appropriately did not insist on the date after the customer challenged it, but could have explained what the retrieved source actually said while distinguishing that from having a shareable document copy.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: What rental yield can I expect? Will price appreciate?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: I wouldn’t want to quote a rental yield or promise price appreciation without verified rental comparables and market data. Pearlmont is freehold, and the stated maintenance fee is RM0.18/sq ft including sinking fund—useful factors when assessing holding costs, but they don’t guarantee returns. Are you mainly looking for rental income or long-term capital growth?

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Bit of both, but mainly rental income with a 5–7 year hold in mind. I’d need to work out net yield after maintenance and vacancy, not just gross. Is the RM0.18 psf fee confirmed for this phase, and where can I check the planned unit supply?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: Yes—the project information lists the Phase 1 maintenance fee at RM0.18/sq ft, inclusive of sinking fund. It also lists 1,846 planned residential units across Towers 1B, 1C and 1D. That’s Pearlmont’s own Phase 1 supply; it doesn’t tell us the competing supply nearby. Are you looking for the local pipeline as well?

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Yes, nearby competing supply and actual rental comps would matter more to me than the facilities list. Do you have a source or catchment breakdown for those, or should I verify them independently? I’ll also check the RM0.18 psf against the phase documents before modelling net yield.

transcript.speaker: system
transcript.request: For the Seberang Jaya catchment, provide any authoritative source or breakdown of planned competing residential supply, with project names, unit counts, status and distance/catchment basis where available. Also provide verified recent rental comparables for similar 3-bedroom units, including source, date, achieved or asking rent, and any known limitations. If no reliable data is available, state that clearly; do not estimate yield.

judge.commercial_progression_evidence: The Agent captured the buyer’s investment purpose and horizon, supplied relevant cost, supply, and price information, and did not push an appointment when the buyer had no viewing intent and later chose to pause. However, the conversation remained an information exchange: after the price response it did not connect the entry cost back to the buyer’s net-performance comparison or test whether a later viewing/location assessment would help. The buyer never indicated that viewing was an appropriate next step.
judge.summary: Human Support answered two valid requests with simulator-only verified fixture evidence, and the Agent remained AI-owned and active throughout. It naturally resumed after the investment-data result, honestly conveyed the lack of verified rental comps and yield data, and used the synthetic RM302,000 starting-price fixture without exceeding its stated conditions. The price response was largely a factual relay rather than a strong continuation of selling. The third request returned no fixture; the Agent disclosed that limitation. The buyer remained NOT_READY and explicitly paused modelling, so no appointment handoff was appropriate. Direct answer to the primary question: support enabled accurate factual continuation, but this conversation does not show reliable movement of a suitable buyer toward Appointment Ready; the buyer’s due diligence remained unresolved and the Agent did not meaningfully test a future viewing step.

improvement_recommendation.recommendation: After an operational answer, connect the result to the buyer’s stated decision criteria and make one proportionate next-step offer when appropriate. When retrieved Knowledge states a document source or date but no shareable copy is available, distinguish those two facts clearly. No Brain or Knowledge change is recommended from this simulator run.
